videos.title: Visual Hierarchy
videos.why: Colour and contrast, size, and grouping, the three main levers, in under four minutes; listen for how each one answers a different question for the reader (what matters most, and what belongs together).

videos.title: Refactoring UI: Bad About
videos.why: Steve Schoger redesigns a real topic page step by step, reorganising content, building a hierarchy and fixing the type; pause before each change and guess what he will de-emphasise next.

podcasts.episode: 74: Steve Schoger - Tactical Design Advice for Developers
podcasts.why: Five practical habits for developers designing their own products; listen for 'designing in greyscale', which forces you to build hierarchy from size, weight and spacing before colour can rescue it.

reads.title: Visual Hierarchy in UX: Definition
reads.why: Colour, scale and grouping with real examples, plus a section on the squint test; do the squint test on your own home page straight after reading.

reads.title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading: Misunderstood, But Still Relevant
reads.why: Corrects a common myth by showing that people fall into the F-pattern when a page lacks structure, and that it works against them; read the alternatives, such as the layer-cake pattern that clear headings produce.

reads.title: Labels are a last resort
reads.why: A two-minute lesson on why 'Label: value' layouts flatten hierarchy, and how '12 left in stock' beats 'In stock: 12'; check your own dashboards for this pattern.
